correctness.rationale: For any m,n≥3 the forward distance on Z_m×Z_n is d((a,b),(i,j))=(i−a mod m)+(j−b mod n). Solid resolution is the two-sided ordered-pair strict distance condition. Assume m≤n. Pairs (i,j) versus (i,j−1) force at least one landmark in each y-row, |S|≥n. Comparing p=(a−1,j) and q=(a,j−1), d(s,q)−d(s,p) is 0,−m,n,n−m depending on x=a and y=j; resolving q from p forces x=a,y≠j, hence at least two y-locations in every x-column, |S|≥2m. For sufficiency an expanding S occupies all rows and each k-column proper cyclic interval intersects at least k+1 distinct y-rows. Modular difference formula d(s,v)−d(s,u)=Δ+δ−m 1_{X+Δ≥m}−n 1_{Y+δ≥n} resolves all ordered pairs: if Δ+δ≤m, at most δ forbidden rows in an interval of m−Δ columns, so one unobstructed landmark; other cases by a chosen row/column. Explicit S={(j mod m,j)} for n≥2m and diagonal+second-row families for m≤n<2m attain max(n,2m). Coordinate swap handles all. Endpoint n=m included. Note no forced vertices by translation and β<mn.
